accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS F-LE.1a–c and F-LE.3 wording (equal differences over equal intervals vs equal factors; an increasing exponential eventually exceeds a linear function). Every number recomputed in node: 1p doubled daily totals (2^d − 1)p, so day 17 = £1,310.71 < £1,700 and day 18 = £2,621.43 > £1,800; day 30 = £10,737,418.23 vs £3,000. First x ≥ 1 with 2^x > mx is 6, 10, 14 for m = 10, 100, 1000 (64 > 60, 1024 > 1000, 16384 > 14000). 80 halved 8 times = 0.3125; 80 − 10 × 8 = 0. Table ratios 8/5 = 1.6, 11/8 = 1.375, 81/90 = 0.9, 9/4 = 2.25.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips from the F-LE literature and GCSE examiner reports: any rising or falling table read as exponential or as linear (100, 90, 81 decay; 7, 12, 17 'keeps growing'), every percentage read as exponential (4% of a FULL charge is linear) and percent of the current value read as linear (car −15%, town +3%), squares mistaken for either, believing a large coefficient keeps a line ahead (500x, 1000x), and expecting repeated halving to reach zero.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaglinexp is built on comparing two growth models side by side: tappable gaps that show difference and ratio together, a fixed-amount vs fixed-percent situation sort, the £100-a-day vs 1p-doubled running totals race, a slope that grows ten-fold while 2^x overtakes it each time, and minus-10 vs halving decay bars. flaggrow builds one exponential from a and b; flagexpg reads one exponential graph; neither compares against a linear model. Shingle overlap gate passed under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule before it is stated: revealing gaps shows +3 +3 +3 against ×1.6 ×1.38 so the equal column decides the call; the race shows the doubling curve lying flat for 17 days then passing; the overtake step makes the line 10 times steeper and the crossing only moves from x = 6 to 10 to 14, which is the 'eventually exceeds any linear function' idea; the decay bars leave 0.31 when the linear bar hits 0. The done text confirms each idea afterwards.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong answer that the task then disproves: 100, 90, 81 as linear 'because it goes down steadily' (gaps show −10, −9, −8.1); 4% of a full charge as exponential 'because it is a percentage'; £100 a day 'starts far ahead' (passed on day 18); a 10× steeper line taking '10 times as long' (it takes 4 more steps); and halving 80 reaching 0 after 8 halvings (it is 0.31).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each naming the slip: 'growing is not enough' for 7, 12, 17, 22; '3% of the current population' for treating 3% growth as +3; 'CURRENT value, not first year' for simple-interest thinking; '2^13 = 8192 beats 6500' for trusting the 500 coefficient; 'differences 4, 12, 36 are not equal' for 2, 6, 18, 54 → 90; and 'multiplying by 0.6 never gives 0' for the bounce. Table classification misses have eight cause-specific messages.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py readability passed: kid text FK 2.6 (limit 6.5), adult text FK 7.4 (limit 9.5). Kid paragraphs carry one example each (5, 10, 15, 20; 3, 6, 12, 24; the battery vs the car; £1,800 vs £2,621 on day 18). Curriculum terms kept precise: linear, exponential, common difference, ratio, growth factor, exponential decay, asymptote in the adult text.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and the explanation is under the 12% overlap limit against flaggrow, flagexpg and flagrexp lessons. Every sentence either states the difference/ratio rule, a worked number or a named mistake; the adult text lists standards, terms, mistakes and what each lab step does; the family tip gives a concrete fold-the-paper vs stack-coins comparison with the 20-step outcome.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark for every step before and after Show me. Five table cells and four gap chips fit across with ratios like ×2.25 readable; the Linear / Exponential / Neither boxes are full-width tap targets; the race and overtake graph labels were moved off the curves after the first screenshots; the decay bars and values fit with room to spare. Buttons wrap under the canvas without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every Show me completed, the challenge rendered, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark, and there were no console or page errors. Every canvas action has a button twin (Show all gaps, Linear, Exponential, Neither, ◀ Day, Day ▶, x ± 1, Take a step) and the canvas aria-label reads each gap's difference and ratio, each day's totals and each overtaking point.
